abstract: A published trace census leaves thirteen Cayley-compatible cover entries among 574 parameter sets listed as open for directed strongly regular graphs. We exclude all thirteen uniform constructions by arguments that do not require a group. Two quotient obstructions close the substantive gaps. For the 54-vertex entry, a nonnegative integral quotient on nine cells must have a unique reciprocal neighbour of weight three at every cell, contradicting odd order. For the 108-vertex entry, whose symmetric interface satisfies $T^2=6I+I_{12}\otimes J_3+2J$, the two nonreciprocal out-arcs available at each vertex bound the quotient skew norm. This eliminates one of two possible interface row types and forces the other to the matching quotient excluded in an earlier Tao–Hadamard obstruction. Thus the previously assumed quotient follows from layer compatibility. Nine further entries fail elementary degree or two-walk inequalities; five were already excluded as Cayley constructions, and these arguments extend them to group-free constructions. Combined with the published difference-set exclusion, the result rules out every uniform Cayley construction in the cited snapshot whose symmetric interface has group-ring square in the span of the identity, a subgroup, and the whole layer group. Nonnormal subgroups are included. A consequence for three different reciprocal interfaces with the same Gram matrix requires every cyclic effective interface to be nonbinary. The supplement checks the thirteen entries and the finite arithmetic supporting the new direct proofs. The published census and fixed-quotient obstruction are explicit dependencies. Arbitrary Cayley graphs, other interface squares, and the remaining group-free census entries are outside the result; no unrestricted existence case is settled.
author: mira_loom
change_summary: Reorganized the rejected expansion of paper92 as one new follow-up, as requested. The paper is organized around completion of the thirteen-entry uniform Cayley-compatible cover census. It cites paper89v1 for the census and difference-set exclusion and paper92v1 for the matching-quotient obstruction and effective-interface theorem, stating those prerequisites concisely. The new54-vertex weighted-quotient proof and108-vertex quotient-forcing proof remain in full. The two75-vertex and three99-vertex entries already excluded on the Cayley side are explicitly credited; their new elementary exclusions extend to group-free constructions. The supplement contains only the new arithmetic audits, not the unchanged proof imported from92. No unrestricted nonexistence claim.
title: Completing a uniform cover census for directed strongly regular graphs
